### 💡 Codex Review Here are some automated review suggestions for this pull request. **Reviewed commit:** `ddf7800c1a`
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
Codex has been enabled to automatically review pull requests in this repo. Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. When you [sign up for Codex through ChatGPT](https://openai.com/codex), Codex can also answer questions or update the PR, like "@codex address that feedback".
I feel like this PR just needs to be deployed to a devnet node and a feat group and let AI check if there are issues with it before we review it
@lodekeeper can you please review this code to see if it causes any regression for post-fulu (ie. current mainnet) or gloas, also check comments added in the pr against our agent.md policy

No regression found for post-fulu (current mainnet) or gloas. What I checked on 258d7d1:

- Fulu block inputs are still `BlockInputColumns`, and gloas still uses `BlockInputNoData` plus `PayloadEnvelopeInput`. The new `PreData` to `NotRequired` mapping in `verifyBlocksDataAvailability` only applies to deneb..electra.
- `engine_newPayload` versioned hashes come from the same body commitments that `BlockInputColumns.getVersionedHashes()` used. Gloas returns at the `isBlockInputNoData` check before that line.
- `publishBlockV2` computes fulu columns exactly as before, and gloas still publishes its columns with the envelope.
- Range and by-root sync keep the column, envelope and parent-payload paths unchanged. `GetBlobsTracker` still sends fulu column inputs and gloas `PayloadEnvelopeInput` to getBlobsV2.
- The removed req/resp protocols and gossip topics are deprecated after `FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS`. That has passed on every network in `chainConfig/networks`, gnosis and chiado included. No src references to the removed symbols remain.

One coverage caveat: `multiFork.test.ts` and `mixedClient.test.ts` still set `FULU_FORK_EPOCH: Infinity`, so those sims exercise electra, not fulu. They pass because no sim sends blob transactions.

Leftovers that could go in this PR:
- `duplicateBlobCount` and `createdByBlob` in `metrics/metrics/lodestar.ts` lost their only increment sites, and `dashboards/lodestar_beacon_chain.json` still graphs `duplicate_blob`.
- The `PreFulu` early return in `getDataColumnSidecarsFromExecution` (`util/execution.ts`) can't be reached anymore, since its only caller now filters non-column inputs first.

The AGENTS.md comment findings are inline. `index.ts:134` and `.ethspecify.yml` already have threads.

Rechecked at 165e7335c6. 7322e2da4d and 165e7335c6 address my four comments. The commitment-keyed pre-fulu reject, the `getBlobs` switch with computed cell proofs, and the two new publish tests look right, and the fix commits add no post-fulu or gloas regressions. CI is green apart from the shared-runner Benchmark job. I'm holding the approval until the plain pre-fulu reject from the open thread lands after #10558.

The plain pre-fulu reject in 788f6be2af looks right, and moving the sims and e2e configs to fulu at genesis is what it needs.

The failing Mixed clients sim is real, but the cause isn't in this PR's code. Moving the sim to `FULU_FORK_EPOCH: 0` exposes a genesis bug: Lodestar's `initializeBeaconStateFromEth1` never sets `proposer_lookahead`, so a fulu-at-genesis state keeps it all zeros. The pyspec genesis helper (`create_genesis_state`) does set it, via `initialize_proposer_lookahead`. In the sim artifacts, the Lodestar beacon prepares and produces every slot of epochs 0-1 with `proposerIndex=0`. Lighthouse rejects those blocks with `IncorrectBlockProposer { block: 0, local_shuffling: 23 }` (slot 1) and `44` (slot 2). Peers drop and the heads diverge from slot 2. Unstable still passes this sim with fulu at epoch 1, because `upgradeStateToFulu` initializes the lookahead.

Lodestar-only sims don't notice, since every node reads the same zeros. I'll open a separate fix for the genesis lookahead and link it here.
